params.body:
"Kunnen we er niks aan doen of niet beter behandelen?" — for this one the handling was already right and the reporting was wrong.

remove.bg answering "Could not identify foreground in image" is not a failure. It is a valid answer to a hard photo, and R S1-6.8 has said so for a while: the original is written as the "cut out" version, the sheet keeps a picture and the job carries on. That branch does exactly that.

It ended with `report($e)`. So a thing that worked as designed was filed as an exception, and on 21 September the error list showed **23 occurrences affecting five dealers** for it — in the very list used to spot what is actually broken. That is the second time today a list cried wolf: five already-fixed issues were still standing open this afternoon for the same reason.

It is now an ordinary log line with the photo and the file. Any **other** answer from remove.bg stays a fault, keeps its `report()` and keeps logging `errors[0].title` — the test pins that line, because without it this would not be tidying up but hiding.

R S1-6.8 now says what happens, why it is not a fault, and what the count was that made it visible.
params.title: A photo without a foreground is not a fault
